findings.text: request_key reads a `section` key that the transition rows never carry — the classified snapshot emits project, session, plan and node and nothing else at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:2333-2346 — so all(parts) is always false on the rows that reach the refusal branch and the key falls back to run_id, making the request-keyed branch dead; behaviour stays correct only because reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2008 re-queues under the same run id, so the docstring's claim that the four fields plus session name a request is untrue of the rows it reads.

the fixture adds `section` to every row, a field the real fleet-transition row does not carry, so test_a_requeue_under_a_fresh_pointer_id_is_the_same_request passes on a row shape production never emits and does not guard the path it names; an assertion added to prevent a regression must be checked by reinstating that regression against a production-shaped row.

request_key duplicates the request-identity capability the repository already owns in reckon/crew/runs.py:545 and reckon/crew/dispatch_refusals.py:84, and contradicts runs.py's deliberate exclusion of the session, so two definitions of the same request now disagree in one codebase.

the landing record says what changed is all in reckon/crew/ticker.py, omitting the recovery_classification.py edit in the same diff, and says the memory is remembered per run two clauses before describing it as keyed on the request.

the population claim of a 63-file arm (base 787 passed, head 792) has no log under the run directory, while the done-when requires every log to sit there and start with its revision and literal command, so the claim rests on the worker's account rather than an artefact a reviewer can open.

item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names a follower-driven test, a negative control, a base arm and pytest -n 8; the test (8 passed), both suite logs and both red controls are recorded, but the importing-files arm is prose-only and no arm used -n 8.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that a refused queued launch is not drawn as a drop; reckon/crew/ticker.py:2131-2150 suppresses the withdrawal row and ticker.py:2292 names the refusal on the request's own row.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it states 8 passed, both suite logs, the negative-control log, the scope_note and 0 added failures, though its tests: line is prose rather than a literal command.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff edits reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py outside the declared fence, recorded in the manifest's scope_note as a prior-review-directed extension; the other three changed paths are inside.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_requeued_refusal_draws_no_dropped_row.py:219-237 guards the fresh-pointer case only because its fixture passes `section` at line 43, a key the production row never carries, so reverting request_key to run_id at ticker.py:2299 would still pass; the both-clauses case at line 253 does redden if ticker.py:606 stops accepting the session prefix.
justifications.evidence: the recorded arms at suite-base.log and suite-after.log reconcile (0 added failures) but run tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py, which imports neither changed module, while the done-when's importing-files arm and its 787/792 figures are claimed at fragment:27 with no log on disk.
justifications.fit: the added names (queued_refusal, request_key, _clause_line, QUEUED_REFUSED_FIELD, REFUSAL_STAGE) follow the mechanism-naming and module-constant idiom already used by SUBMISSION_STAGE and LIFT_STAGE at reckon/crew/ticker.py:279-281, with no plan label or ticket reference.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/ticker.py:2292-2320 recognises a refused queued launch and prints it once on the request's own row while keeping the word queued, which is the goal the incident drew a drop for.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/ticker.py:623 request_key re-implements the request identity already owned by reckon/crew/runs.py:545 _node_identity and reckon/crew/dispatch_refusals.py:84 rather than extending either, and includes session where runs.py deliberately excludes it; the _clause_line helper at ticker.py:3563 does correctly extend the shared clause-row layout.
justifications.scope_discipline: reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:130-140 is edited outside the fence declared at prompt.txt:80-86, disclosed in the manifest's scope_note and limited to hoisting the two prefixes its own composer already wrote.
